title: Where are Bellingham's most haunted spots? Find out on these spooky tours
byline: Bellingham HeraldFollowJulia HawkinsThu, October 29, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTCAdd to Preferred Sources
excerpt: Charles Crooks has been sharing ghost stories and local history since 2023.
content:
Do you believe in ghosts?

A local business takes locals and visitors on tours of Bellingham's downtown and Fairhaven districts to reveal some of the city's most haunted spots and buildings.

Bellingham Ghost Tours draws its inspiration from Bellingham's history as well as founder Charlie Crook's personal past.

As someone with a lifelong fascination with the paranormal and unexplained, Crooks said he's "experienced some energies that I would call weird or uncomfortable."

"But I've never been hurt with anything," he told The Bellingham Herald.

Here's what folks curious about Bellingham's haunted past should know:

How did Bellingham Ghost Tours begin?

When Crooks moved to Bellingham in 2009, he was searching for ways to meet new people.

An amateur ghost hunter, he joined the Bellingham Observers of the Odd. The former organization visited led ghost haunting trips in building that had unexplainable occurrences

"It was just (a) very amateur group, just people going out for fun, and I did well," Crooks told The Bellingham Herald in a video interview. "That was my start of official ghost hunting,"

The COVID-19 pandemic put an impromptu halt to Crooks' ghost hunting. He initially had no intention of returning to extraterrestrial activity.

Then The Good Time Girls reached out in 2023.

The company, which provides guided walking tours of Bellingham, says it specializes in "off-beat history served with signature sass."

"(The Good Time Girls) reached out and said, 'Hey, we have a lot of interest coming our way about haunted things in the area. Would you start something for that?' " Crooks recalled. "I said, 'All right, I could dig deep into my past here.' "

That marked the start of Bellingham Ghost Tours' Fairhaven tour.

"It's just grown since there," Crooks said.

He created the Downtown Ghost Tour in 2023 after Bellingham's Chuckanut Bay Distillery reached out.

Distillery staff claimed to have paranormal experiences and asked Crooks to create a tour examining unexplained occurrences in Bellingham.

Today, Crooks offers two tours for ghost enthusiasts and history buffs, sharing stories of Bellingham's past.

He also gives private tarot card readings.

What can I see on a local ghost tour?

Bellingham Ghost Tours' Fairhaven tour starts just outside of Sycamore Square, which Crooks said is "the most haunted building in Bellingham."

On a recent weekend evening, he started by sharing stories of Sycamore Square shop owners' experiences of paranormal activities.

According to Crooks, employees in 12th Street Shoes have reported hearing and seeing shoes suddenly dropping and shifting after customers had left for the evening.

Meanwhile, a music teacher who used to hold classes in the building told Crooks that candy would suddenly go missing from a bowl intended for students.

Other stops during the Fairhaven ghost tour included Finnegan's Alley, Village Green and the former Fairhaven Terminal Building.

At some stops, Crooks showed tour participants photos of small white orbs, spectral silhouettes and ghostly figures, signifying the possible presence of the paranormal.

Crooks played audio recordings at Finnegan's Alley and Village Green, challenging people on the tours to decode what spirits may be saying.

In one recording, a female voice could be heard whispering, "This is fun."

Are Bellingham buildings really haunted?

How does Crooks determine if a location is actually haunted?

"You can tell when someone's being genuine or not," he said, adding that he starts from a place of belief. "There are a lot of very wild claims that end up being true."

"I believe, as humans, we can leave behind energy, and that can get trapped in time in all sorts of different ways," he explained.

When he encounters what he suspects is a supernatural presence, "I'm usually trying to figure if there is something intelligent and if it can respond to us," Crooks said. "That'll usually determine what happens after."

Crooks asks tour participants to keep an open mind.

"If we can just share our experiences and why we believe what we believe, I'm all for," Crooks said. "When you have a stick in the mud where people that are just looking to disprove, that's where I have the hardest time with it."

Most people are excited to explore Bellingham's connection to the paranormal, he said.

"I feel like there's something else in the world we can't really explain," one tour attendee, Leah Talley, told The Herald. "I don't know what else we call it, but I'd like to believe it's ghosts."

"I believe the ghosts just wanna hang out. They wanna have fun," said another tour attendee, Makenna LaCombs.

What do reviewers say?

Bellingham Ghost tours has a five-star rating on Google Reviews.

Reviewer Roni Leonard called the tour was "fantastic".

"(Crooks is) engaging and has great knowledge of the area's haunted history!" Leonard wrote in her May 2026 review. "We even stayed and got readings, and they were all spot on!"

How much do ghost tours cost?

All Bellingham Ghost Tours events cost $27.50 a person.

The Downtown and Fairhaven tours are normally offered at 7:30 p.m. and 9:30 p.m. on Friday and Saturday all year round.

To celebrate the spooky season, tours will be daily at various times in preparation for Halloween. The tours will be at noon, 1, 7 and 9 p.m. until Nov. 1st. After that, tours will occur on Fridays and Saturdays at 7 and 9p.m.

You can also book a private tarot card reading for $25.

Tickets can be booked on the Bellingham Ghost Tours website.
